quiz.question: 1. Which strategy is commonly used to generate short URL codes from unique numeric identifiers?
options: Password hashing as the lookup key
quiz.explanation: Base62 encoding (using [0-9a-zA-Z]) turns unique 64-bit auto-incrementing or Snowflake numeric IDs into compact URL-safe 7-character strings (62^7 ≈ 3.52 trillion combinations) without collisions.

quiz.question: 2. When should a chat server acknowledge that a message has been durably accepted?
options: After the required durable persistence operation succeeds
Only after every group member reads it
quiz.explanation: Store-first persistence is required: a chat server must write the message to durable database/replicated storage before returning an ACK to the sender. In-memory ACKs risk silent data loss during crashes.

quiz.question: 3. Why is exactly-once delivery difficult for notifications?
options: The sender and provider may disagree about whether an attempt succeeded
Database transactions automatically cover external email providers
quiz.explanation: External third-party providers (APNs, SendGrid, Twilio) cannot participate in distributed 2PC transactions. Network timeouts or lost ACKs leave delivery state ambiguous, mandating at-least-once delivery with idempotency keys.

quiz.question: 4. What is the main problem with fan-out-on-write for an account with millions of followers?
options: It makes all feed reads impossible
One post can trigger an enormous number of feed-entry writes
quiz.explanation: A user with 10 million followers causes 10 million write operations in follower inboxes on every single post (write amplification), exhausting queue capacity and worker threads.

quiz.question: 5. What is a transactional outbox used for?
options: Making a database update and its event-publication intent durable together
quiz.explanation: The transactional outbox pattern commits business entity modifications and the corresponding notification event into the same database transaction, preventing split-brain inconsistencies between DB and message brokers.

quiz.question: 6. Which API pagination approach is often suitable for large, continuously updated feeds?
quiz.explanation: Cursor pagination (keyset pagination using (created_at, post_id) < ($timestamp, $id)) avoids missing/duplicate posts when new items arrive at the top and executes in O(1) index seek time unlike O(N) OFFSET scans.

quiz.question: 7. Which component should remain the authoritative source for whether a private social post is accessible?
options: The trusted source of current post visibility and authorization rules
quiz.explanation: Cached feed timelines only store lightweight references (post IDs). The core post/authorization service must validate current privacy permissions and post deletion status during post hydration.

quiz.question: 8. Which notification design is best suited to handling an external provider outage?
options: Make every business request wait indefinitely
Persist pending work, bound retries, monitor the queue, and handle failed jobs
quiz.explanation: Decoupled asynchronous worker queues with exponential backoff + jitter, bounded retry thresholds, circuit breakers, and Dead-Letter Queues (DLQ) isolate external provider outages from upstream business flows.
